name: Krangket Island
bio: Road-free island a five-minute boat ride from Madang, with two villages, gardens and a lagoon beach.
note: Island: five-minute boat trip from Madang; two villages with gardens, a lagoon beach and a basic lodge.

facts.text: Krangket Island is a five-minute boat trip from the small boat terminal in Madang; boats leave every half hour and cost 2 kina.
Two villages with gardens and hedges, no roads, a lagoon beach and Krangket Lodge (two bungalows, 80 kina a night, bring your own food).

name: Karkar Island
bio: Oval volcanic island in the Bismarck Sea with an active twin-caldera volcano and a mountain view down to Madang.
note: Island: volcanic island 30 km off Madang with a caldera volcano (last big eruptions 1974-75), a ring road and views back to Madang; known for bilums.

facts.text: An oval volcanic island about 25 km by 19 km in the Bismarck Sea, with an active volcano having two nested calderas at its centre.
Eruptions in 1974-75 covered about 70% of the inner caldera floor; the 1979 eruption killed two volcanologists.
The island is known for the view from its mountain down to Madang town, and its fertile volcanic soil is farmed for food and cash crops.

name: Lae
bio: Papua New Guinea's second city and Morobe's capital, where the Highlands Highway starts, with a botanic garden.
note: Town: PNG's second city and Morobe's capital, at the start of the Highlands Highway; gateway to the Highlands and Huon Gulf.

name: Lae War Cemetery
bio: Commonwealth WWII cemetery beside Lae Botanic Gardens, begun in 1944 and holding the Lae Memorial to the missing.
note: Cemetery: Commonwealth war cemetery with about 2,800 WWII burials, next to the botanic gardens and including the Lae Memorial.

facts.text: Contains 2,818 Commonwealth burials of the Second World War, 444 of them unidentified, per Wikivoyage; the Commission's own figure for identified casualties is lower.
Begun in 1944 by the Australian Army Graves Service and taken over by the Commission in 1947, beside the Lae Botanic Gardens; the Lae Memorial for Australians with no known grave stands inside.

name: Rainforest Habitat
bio: Walk-through rainforest aviary with birds of paradise at Unitech in Lae; reported run-down, so check before going.
note: Wildlife: 10-hectare animal and bird display at Lae University of Technology, with about 80 birds of paradise in a rainforest enclosure.

facts.text: About 3,000 sq m of reconstructed rainforest inside a walk-through aviary under an 11 m canopy, with further enclosures, on the grounds of the PNG University of Technology.
Wikivoyage reports around 80 birds of paradise on display, from a dozen of PNG's 30 species.
Lonely Planet names a large saltwater crocodile as the star but reports collapsing walkways and derelict enclosures.
A Unitech PMV from Eriku drops at Gate No. 2, or it is a 15-minute walk from the main gate.
Run by Unitech Development & Consultancy; contact +675 473 4344.

name: Wau
bio: Gold-rush town at about 1,100 m, the inland end of the Black Cat Track, with the Wau Ecology Institute nearby.
note: Town: gold-rush town at about 1,100 m, the Black Cat Track's inland end, with the Wau Ecology Institute nearby.

name: Bulolo
bio: Former gold-dredging town on the Bulolo River, 32 km north-west of Wau, with dredge relics and a golf course.
note: Town: former gold-dredging town on the Bulolo River, 32 km north-west of Wau, with dredge relics and a golf course.

name: Bulolo Gold Dredges
bio: Gold dredges left in the Bulolo jungle, every part airlifted in by Junkers aircraft before dredging ended in 1965.
note: Relic: eight 2,000-tonne gold dredges airlifted into the Bulolo valley; some abandoned in the valley and still visible (Wikivoyage).

facts.text: Eight 2,000-tonne gold dredges were built for the Bulolo River; every part was airlifted into the valley using Junkers aircraft.

Dredging stopped in June 1965 after turning over 7.4 million cubic metres; one dredge was cut up to make bridges, two went to South America, and the rest in varying condition can still be seen abandoned in the jungle.
OSM maps two Gold Dredge attractions south-east of Bulolo town at about -7.248, 146.668.

name: Tavurvur
bio: Active volcano above Rabaul reached by road, with hot springs and ash deposits; climbs start here with a guide.
note: Volcano: active stratovolcano above Rabaul with a drive-up parking point, hot springs and ash views; Wikivoyage 'See' item 1.

facts.fact: Active volcano reached by road; a parking lot where you pay, hot springs (deadly hot), views of ash deposits and volcano, and handicraft sellers; climbs start here
Tavurvur and Vulcan erupted on 19 September 1994 and covered most of Rabaul in ash

name: Kokopo
bio: East New Britain's current provincial capital and airport gateway, with markets and a war museum.
note: Town: current provincial capital and airport gateway (Tokua), with markets and the Kokopo war museum; covered in Wikivoyage 'Rabaul'.

name: Rabaul Volcano Observatory
bio: Volcano observatory on Mount Tavanabatir with a lookout over Rabaul town, the bay and the volcano.
note: Lookout: volcano observatory on Mount Tavanabatir with a view over Rabaul town, bay and volcano; Wikivoyage 'See' item 6 and 'Do' climb.

facts.fact: Observatory on Mount Tavanabatir; its monitoring is credited with no deaths in the 1994 eruption; lookout with a view over town, bay and volcano
Reached by a very narrow paved road beside a white cross; free per listing

name: Japanese Barge Tunnel
bio: WWII tunnel near Mount Vulcan with Japanese barges still inside, down a rough unmarked track at Karavia.
note: WWII tunnel: Japanese tunnel near Mount Vulcan with barges still inside at Karavia; Wikivoyage 'See' item 3.

facts.fact: Around 700 km of Japanese tunnels in the hills round Simpson Harbour; barges can still be seen in this tunnel at Karavia
Down a short rough unmarked track near Mt Vulcan

name: New Guinea Club Museum
bio: 1937 New Guinea Club building turned museum of Rabaul's history, with many photographs, opposite Yamamoto's bunker.
note: Museum: 1937 New Guinea Club building now a museum of Rabaul's history, with photographs; Wikivoyage 'See' item 5.

facts.fact: The 1937 New Guinea Club, now a museum of Rabaul's history with many photos (very hot); Yamamoto's bunker lies opposite

name: Bitapaka War Cemetery
bio: Commonwealth war cemetery near Kokopo for WWII servicemen from many countries, with a Japanese war memorial.
note: War cemetery: Australian War Graves Commission cemetery for WWII servicemen of many nations, with a Japanese war memorial; Wikivoyage 'See' item 2.

facts.fact: Maintained by the Australian War Graves Commission/CWGC as the resting place of servicemen from many countries; Japanese war memorial at a former sea-plane base; free
CWGC lists 652 identified casualties; the Rabaul Memorial to the Missing commemorates over 1,200 Australians with no known grave

name: Kokopo War and Cultural Museum
bio: Museum in central Kokopo of Japanese war relics, with a few photographs, opposite the waterfront golf course.
note: Museum: Japanese war relics and photographs in central Kokopo; Wikivoyage 'See' item 7.

facts.fact: Collection of Japanese war relics and a few photographs and trinkets, opposite the waterfront golf course in central Kokopo

name: Duke of York Islands
bio: Group of 13 islands about 45 minutes by boat from Kokopo, visited for diving, snorkelling and picnics.
note: Island group: 45 minutes by boat from Kokopo, for diving, snorkelling and picnics; PNG Tourism 'East New Britain' page.

facts.fact: 13 islands, 58 sq km, including Duke of York, Makada, Kabakon, Kerawara, Ulu, Mioko and Mualim
Hotels organise sea tours including diving and the Duke of York Islands; tours start around K700 per car for land tours

name: Kimbe Bay
bio: Bay off Kimbe with over 900 fish and 400 coral species, reached by dive boat from Kimbe or Walindi.
note: Dive area: bay with 400+ coral and 900+ fish species, WWII wrecks and dolphins; Wikivoyage 'Kimbe' Do (diving).

facts.fact: More than 900 fish and 400 coral species identified; best diving mid-August to late December and February to May/June; chance of swimming with dolphins
Walindi Plantation Resort says its day boats reach more than 40 dive sites and calls the bay a Mission Blue Hope Spot
Dive packages are sold by the resorts; the resort page lists no single day price

name: Owers' Corner
bio: Southern trailhead of the 96 km Kokoda Track, 50 km from Port Moresby; treks need a licensed operator and permit.
note: Trail start/end: the southern trailhead at Owers' Corner (Central Province, 50 km east of Port Moresby) with the monument where the track starts; every guided walk begins or ends here.

facts.fact: Southern end of the 96 km Kokoda Track, 50 km from Port Moresby; treks run 6-10 days either direction
International trekker permit K350; PNG residents K175; trek must be arranged with a licensed operator, and operators include the permit in their price

name: Isurava
bio: Site of the 1942 Battle of Isurava on the Kokoda Track, with a memorial and museum reached only on foot.
note: Battle site and village: the Isurava war memorial and museum on the track, the site of the 1942 Battle of Isurava; Wikivoyage notes it is hard not to weep at the memorial site.

facts.fact: Site of the Battle of Isurava, 26-31 August 1942; present site is north of the wartime village
One of four official track museums (Efogi, Kokoda, Isurava Memorial, Alola), open only if the key holder is around
International trekker permit K350

name: Kokoda
bio: Station town at the northern end of the Kokoda Track, with the only airfield on the track and the finish of most walks.
note: Town: station town at the northern end of the Kokoda Track, the only airfield on the track, and the finishing point of most walks.

name: Popondetta
bio: Oro Province capital and gateway, with flights from Port Moresby and the road to Kokoda; a base rather than a sight.
note: Town: the Oro Province capital and gateway, with Girua Airport flights from Port Moresby and the road to Kokoda; the tourism site calls it a base rather than a sight.

name: Tufi
bio: Fishing and dive town on the Cape Nelson peninsula, the base for the Tufi fjords, reef dives and tapa-cloth making.
note: Town: fishing and dive town on the Cape Nelson peninsula, base for the Tufi fjords, reef dives and tapa-cloth making; Wikivoyage calls it the Fjordland of Papua New Guinea.

name: Buna
bio: Coastal Oro Province village with WWII relics and a memorial plaque to the 32nd Red Arrow Division at its entrance.
note: Village: coastal village and the Kokoda Track trailhead, with WWII relics and a memorial plaque to the 32nd Division; the tourism site says to visit Buna and Gona.

facts.fact: Memorial plaque at the village entrance dedicated to Herman Bottcher and the 32nd Red Arrow Division
PNG-owned operator Buna Treks and Tours is among Kokoda Track operators

name: Gona
bio: Coastal village in Oro Province where Japanese forces landed in 1942; visited for WWII relics, with a local guide.
note: Village: coastal village and WWII battle site where Japanese forces landed in 1942; the tourism site names it with Buna as a place to visit WWII relics.

facts.fact: Coastal village in Oro Province, site of the Japanese landing in 1942
PNG Tourism suggests visiting Buna and Gona for WWII relics

name: Wewak
bio: East Sepik's capital and the gateway for Sepik River trips, with a wartime Japanese airbase and surrender site.
note: Town: provincial capital of East Sepik and the gateway for Sepik River trips and the Wewak islands; WWII Japanese airbase and surrender site.

name: Vanimo
bio: Sandaun Province capital on the Indonesian border, the base for nearby surf breaks and coastal headlands.
note: Town: capital of Sandaun Province on the Indonesian border; base for the surf breaks and the coastal headlands.

name: Maprik
bio: Sepik town whose district is known for forward-leaning haus tambaran spirit houses; ask permission before entering.
note: Town and district: the Maprik area holds the best-known haus tambaran spirit houses; Wikipedia article is the district.

facts.fact: PNG Tourism points to the forward-leaning haus tambaran spirit houses at Maprik
District covers 843 sq km per Wikipedia

name: Sepik River
bio: River reached from Wewak by motor-canoe, with day trips, overnight expeditions and village stays.
note: River: the Sepik, PNG's longest river, visited by motor-canoe and riverboat trips to river villages; a long linear feature, pin at its main visitor access (Wewak, Angoram, Pagwi). Pinned at Angoram, a river-town access point, not the river centroid.

facts.fact: Wewak is the main access point to the Sepik, linked by road to Angoram, Timbunke and Pagwi
PNG Tourism lists day trips or overnight expeditions, village stays at Korogu and lodges such as Karawari

name: Kairiru Island
bio: Island 30 minutes by boat from Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs.
note: Island: volcanic island 30 minutes by boat off Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs (PTPA); guesthouse per Wikivoyage. Wikipedia title 'Kairiru' is the language.

facts.fact: Island 30 minutes by boat from Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs
One of four islands within an hour by boat of Wewak

name: Mushu Island
bio: Small island reached by boat from Wewak, one of four within an hour of town.
note: Island: coral atoll with a white-sand beach and reef fish, half an hour off Wewak; basic guesthouse. Named Muschu by PTPA. Wikipedia title is the Disney character.

facts.fact: One of four islands reachable in under an hour by boat from Wewak (spelled Mushu)

name: Cape Wom
bio: Peace park near Wewak where General Adachi signed the Japanese surrender in 1945, with some tunnels still open.
note: WWII memorial: peace park where General Adachi signed the Japanese surrender in New Guinea in 1945, with open Japanese tunnels; PTPA calls it the Wom Memorial and Japanese Peace Park.

facts.fact: Peace park and war memorial where Lt Gen Adachi signed the surrender on 13 September 1945; some Japanese tunnels still open
Listed by PNG Tourism as a place to visit the war memorial

name: Vanimo Surf Breaks
bio: Reef and point breaks west of Vanimo with waves up to 3 m, best September to March and for experienced surfers only.
note: Surf breaks: consistent reef and point breaks west of Vanimo, up to 3 m, best September to March (Wikivoyage); experienced surfers only.

name: Daru
bio: Western Province's capital on Daru Island at the Fly River mouth, the domestic air gateway to the province, mainly for fishing.
note: Town: provincial capital of Western Province on Daru Island at the Fly River mouth, and the domestic air gateway to the province. PNG Tourism calls it the 'Wild Wild West' of PNG; Wikivoyage says it has little to interest visitors beyond fishing. Also covers Daru Island (same island, not a separate spot).

name: Kiunga
bio: River port on the Fly River at the southern end of the Kiunga-Tabubil Highway, a base for birdwatching and nature tours.
note: Town: river port on the Fly River and southern end of the Kiunga-Tabubil Highway, known as a base for birdwatching (Wikivoyage) and for nature tours (Kiunga Nature Tours is based here, per PNG Tourism).

name: Lake Murray
bio: Remote lake and wetland in Western Province for birdwatching and fishing, reached by light aircraft then boat.
note: Natural lake: Papua New Guinea's largest lake (about 647 km2 in the dry season, up to five times that in the wet season), surrounded by wetlands and rainforest. Wikivoyage lists it for birdwatching, fishing and village visits; access is normally by charter aircraft through a lodge.

facts.fact: Lodge has 12 cabins and is reached by light aircraft then boat from the airstrip
Birdwatching and fishing for black bass, barramundi and saratoga; rainy season (Dec-Apr) the lake can grow to about five times its normal size

name: Tonda Wildlife Management Area
bio: Ramsar wetland of 590,000 hectares on the Indonesian border, reached by charter flight to Bensbach Wildlife Lodge.
note: Protected wetland: PNG's largest protected area, a Ramsar site on the Indonesian border with over 250 waterbird species and savanna wildlife. PNG Tourism lists 'Visit the Tonda Wildlife Management Area'; visits are based at Bensbach Wildlife Lodge.

facts.fact: Ramsar wetland designated 16 March 1993, established 1975, 590,000 ha, adjoining Indonesia's Wasur National Park
Bensbach Wildlife Lodge on the Bensbach River is run by Trans Niugini Tours; access by charter flight from Mount Hagen, Port Moresby or Daru
